title: Heartbreaking reason CCTV of a young woman and her teenage brother walking out of a Kmart store means so much to their shattered mum
text:
An anguished mother who lost two of her children in a high -speed horror shock 17 months ago has shared the final images shortly before she died.
The children of Angelina Kauffman, Alina, 24, and Ernesto, 15, were beaten in a collision in front of her home in the southwest of Sydney on September 1, 2023, when a car that was supposedly approximated wrong side of the road.
Only 44 minutes before, the couple was captured in CCTV leaving Kmart in Westfield Liverpool.
Alina had gone there to pick up her brother at the end of her turn, who had just started working there.
Mrs. Kauffman has only returned to the Kmart store twice since her children died.
A visit was to ask the store to track the final images of Alina and Ernesto, which she shared publicly on Tiktok last week.
“When I entered, I was trembling and was crying,” Kauffman said Yahoo .
‘I just wanted to see them alive, because after that the only time I saw them was dead in the morgue. I just wanted to see my children.
Alina (in the photo) and his brother Ernesto were killed in a frontal collision from home on September 1, 2023,
This image of Alina, 24, and Ernesto, 15, leaving Kmart in Westfield Liverpool on the night of September 1, 2023. They were killed only 45 minutes later.
The images showed Alina and Ernesto, who carried their Kmart uniform, leaving the store side by side.
“What attracted me the most is … They are even knowing that this is the last time they are going to drive together, they will eat together,” Kauffman said.
After leaving Westfield Liverpool, Alina led 2.2 km to McDonald’s in Elizabeth Drive, where at 9.14 pm he called her mother and made a joke.
“My daughter called me jokingly saying:” Mom, I couldn’t find my brother. “I said: ‘What?’ , recalled Mrs. Kauffman.
‘I said:’ Ok, I love you, I drive safely ‘, and they told me’ I love you, mom ‘.
That was the last contact with their beloved children.
Six minutes later, the brothers were only 100 meters from their Heckberg house when they were supposedly beaten and killed in Sadleir Avenue.
The driver, Johnson Kokozian, 21 years old at that time, supposedly fled the scene.
Brother and sister Alina (left) and Ernesto (right) are photographed playing together in a park
Alina and Ernesto are photographed in a photograph with their family dog
His license had supposedly disqualified at that time. He remains in prison in prison.
‘I can’t understand why they died, especially in this way. They were so close to home … I just don’t click on my brain, “Kauffman said.
“They were not doing anything wrong, they were very, very good people.”
If they were still alive today, Alina would probably be working as a nurse, while Ernesto would have started the year 12.
I wanted to be a social worker and help families and children, according to their mother.
Mrs. Kauffman wants harder punishments for serious road crimes and has gathered 200,000 signatures for a petition.
The NSW Law Reform Commission has been looking at its submission during the last 10 months, but is frustrated by the slow rhythm of the bureaucracy.
Mrs. Kauffmann said she will not let her children become another road death statistics.
‘I will never stop. I don’t want another family to go through this, this death sentence that has been treated, ” he said.
‘Laws must change, Australia needs to change. Enough is enough.
